module_title: MS Access - Foundational Basics and RDBMS Concepts
introduction: In the 'Computer Knowledge' section of SSC CGL, especially for Tier-2 (Mains), MS Access is a highly tested subject. It is Microsoft's premier 'Database Management System' (DBMS) used to securely store, manage, and link massive amounts of information.

core_concepts.title: What is MS Access?
core_concepts.description: MS Access is an RDBMS (Relational Database Management System). Unlike Word or PowerPoint, it stores data in a structured format across multiple interconnected 'Tables'. It is widely used by small to medium businesses for data management.

core_concepts.title: Table - The Foundation
core_concepts.description: In MS Access, absolutely all data is stored exclusively inside 'Tables'. A table is a grid made up of Rows and Columns.

core_concepts.title: Record (Row / Tuple)
core_concepts.description: A horizontal row in a table is officially called a 'Record'. One record represents the complete set of information about a single entity (e.g., all details of one specific student). In advanced database terminology, a row is also called a 'Tuple'.

core_concepts.title: Field (Column / Attribute)
core_concepts.description: A vertical column in a table is officially called a 'Field'. It represents a specific category of data (e.g., strictly 'Names' or strictly 'Ages'). In advanced database terminology, a column is also called an 'Attribute'.

important_entities.name: File Extension
important_entities.significance: From MS Access 2007 onwards, the default file extension is `.accdb` (Access Database). Prior to 2003, it was `.mdb` (Microsoft Database).

important_entities.name: Database
important_entities.significance: The actual file you create in MS Access is called a 'Database', which acts as a master container that can hold multiple tables inside it.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because both use rows and columns, beginners confuse the two. Remember the distinction: Excel is a 'Spreadsheet' designed for mathematical calculations and charts. Access is a 'Database' designed to securely link and filter millions of records.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Examiners frequently ask for the Access equivalents of standard terms. Always map Row to Record (both start with R) and Column to Field.

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed Tier-1/Tier-2 question format: 'What type of software application is MS Access?' Without hesitation, select 'RDBMS (Relational Database Management System)'.
